Over the past few months I've been building VenHub (Vendor Hub), an operations portal for vendors and internal teams at iForte Solusi Infotek. Field surveys and FTTH preventive maintenance used to run through many manual steps across several systems. VenHub moves that flow into one portal connected directly to Salesforce.

What VenHub does today: 
1. Connectivity Survey Salesforce sends surveys to vendors. Vendors fill in the Survey Form section by section, with photos per group. After submission, Salesforce creates or updates the Work Report and sends the status (Submitted, Approved or Rejected) back to VenHub.
2. Automatic PHS documents When a survey is Approved, the system calculates quantities against the PHS price list, generates the PDF, and uploads it to the Work Report in Salesforce. Failed deliveries retry automatically and can also be resent manually.
3. FTTH Preventive Maintenance Technicians submit a Customer ID, a category, and evidence photos. The photo count is validated against the category. Salesforce then sends the Work Order and Service Appointment status back.

What's next We plan to move more of the FTTH business process into VenHub, so vendors and internal teams work from one place.

Security and personal data protection VenHub holds customer and vendor data, so I built this in from the start, using Indonesia's Personal Data Protection Law (UU PDP) as the reference:
1. Email OTP login, plus mandatory Microsoft Authenticator for Super Admins and Admins
2. Temporary account lock after repeated failed logins, and automatic logout when idle
3. Personal data masked in logs and in views for roles that shouldn't see it
4. Access to personal data recorded: who, which role, which endpoint
5. Automatic data retention for logs, histories and notifications

Tech stack:
1. Backend: Go (Gin), PostgreSQL, JWT, TOTP
2. Frontend: Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui, Zustand, React Hook Form + Zod, acting as a BFF so the browser never handles the API token
3. Integrations: Salesforce (Apex/LWC and REST), internal email service
4. Deployment: Docker & Jenkins

What I learned:
1. Two-way integration needs retries, idempotency, and clear logs, or small failures are hard to trace.
2. Security and privacy cost far less when built in from the beginning.
3. As developers, we have to solve problems, keep learning, and adapt to whatever comes up. We shouldn't idolize a single platform, because a developer needs to see the big picture and pick the tools that will actually help the company.

Thanks to the team who helped along the way Andrey Sholinka, Dwiky Kurniawan, Daffa Asyqar Ahmad Khalisheka, Karina Virgi, Viriya Putta, Jessica Jetje Joanna.

The base case is delay and repricing of AI projects, not cancellation. Operators should file licences early, and SMEs should consider renting AI compute and timing purchases ahead of the 1H27 repricing.

WHY DID HONGFA – THE WORLD'S LEADING ELECTROMAGNETIC RELAY MANUFACTURER – CHOOSE TO ESTABLISH A FACTORY IN VIETNAM?

On November 10, 2026, China's Hongfa Group officially inaugurated its automotive electronic components manufacturing plant, a joint venture with VinFast, in Cat Hai, Hai Phong, Vietnam.

Hongfa is a global leader in electronic component manufacturing, with impressive figures:

▪️ Ranked No. 1 globally in electromagnetic relay market share, according to 2025 industry reports.

▪️ Annual production of over 3.3 billion products.

▪️ Market presence in more than 120 countries and territories.

▪️ Over 18,000 employees worldwide.

▪️ Revenue exceeding RMB 17 billion in 2025.

Why did Hongfa choose Vietnam to expand its global manufacturing footprint?

1. The attraction of anchor manufacturers

Hongfa has been supplying components to VinFast since 2019. After years of cooperation, the group decided to establish local manufacturing operations to serve its customer directly.

2. Supply chain optimization

Locating its factory within VinFast's manufacturing complex enables Hongfa to reduce logistics costs, shorten delivery times and strengthen technical collaboration.

3. Deeper integration into Vietnam's manufacturing ecosystem

Manufacturing in Vietnam not only supports VinFast's localization strategy but also creates opportunities for Hongfa to reach new customers and markets.

4. Increasingly developed industrial infrastructure

By utilizing existing factory facilities, Hongfa significantly shortened its project implementation timeline.

5. Global manufacturing expansion

Vietnam has become Hongfa's third overseas manufacturing location, following Germany and Indonesia.

IS VIETNAM ENTERING A NEW WAVE OF INDUSTRIAL INVESTMENT?

With the continued development of major manufacturers such as Samsung, LG, Foxconn, Intel, Amkor and VinFast, Vietnam is gradually building industrial ecosystems capable of attracting world-leading suppliers.

In the coming years, I expect Vietnam to attract more new manufacturing projects and capacity expansions in semiconductors, electronic components, electric vehicles, precision engineering, automation and supporting industries.

This represents a significant opportunity for Vietnamese manufacturers, local authorities and industrial park developers.

In my view, Vietnam's FDI attraction strategy should focus not only on attracting individual investors but also on attracting entire supply chains and global manufacturing ecosystems.

For manufacturers, the fundamental questions are not simply where to invest, but also whom to manufacture for, whom to sell to, and which supply chains to participate in.

After Hongfa, which other world-leading industrial groups do you think will choose Vietnam to establish new factories or expand their manufacturing operations between 2027 and 2030?

When a ship carries captured CO₂ from one country to another, where does responsibility for reporting emissions change hands?

On 24 November, Singapore and Australia signed an agreement in Canberra to enable CO₂ captured in Singapore to be shipped to Australia for permanent storage beneath the seabed.*

The agreement puts the handover at the point where the CO₂ is first unloaded from the vessel within Australian jurisdiction.

Singapore accounts for emissions associated with the CO₂ stream before that point. Australia takes over at the handover and accounts for emissions from there onward. The same split applies to fugitive emissions.

The quantity and composition of the CO₂ stream must be measured at export and again at handover. The handover measurement determines how much CO₂ passes into Australia’s emissions accounting responsibility.

The agreement takes effect 30 days after the final notification that both countries have completed their domestic procedures. Projects will also need the applicable permits.**

For developers, this turns a reporting rule into a design question. The exporter, ship operator and storage provider need to agree on how they will reconcile the two measurements and what happens if a cargo arrives outside the storage operator’s acceptance limits.

That matters for Indonesia, too. Its June 2025 memorandum with Singapore set out plans for a joint working group to study what a legally binding cross-border CCS agreement would need to cover.***

The Australia–Singapore agreement gives Indonesia a concrete reference for those discussions. For any future route, settling where the handover happens and how the cargo is measured would give project teams a clearer basis for designing terminals, specifying meters and negotiating transport and storage contracts.

 🔎 Always glad to exchange perspectives!

* Singapore Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry, Singapore–Australia cross-border CCS agreement factsheet, 24 November 2026.  
** Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Singapore–Australia Transboundary CCS Agreement, Articles 1, 3–5 and 11.  
*** Singapore Ministry of Trade and Industry, press release on the signing of three memoranda with Indonesia, 13 June 2025.

"Will the Nvidia fallout kill off Asia’s data centre boom?
Projects that touted chip access to Chinese customers face tighter US scrutiny

After #JensenHuang’s abrupt return to the helm of Nvidia, big questions still loom over south-east Asia’s data centres, which have benefited from voracious demand for top-end AI chips but face tougher US export rules.

Countries such as Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia have received hundreds of billions of dollars of #investment from tech giants and#datacentre developers, as the region becomes one of the fastest-growing hubs for#AI infrastructure.

But new restrictions from Washington this month aimed at closing a loophole that allowed Chinese companies to use American#chips in south-east Asian data centres have put much of that investment in jeopardy.

The new rules — which were announced as US authorities investigate Singaporean business Megaspeed over alleged smuggling of Nvidia chips to China — have the potential to cause legal complications, financing issues and due diligence concerns for hundreds of projects under development.

The financial implications are far-reaching. Banks,#privateequity firms, creditors and tech groups have committed billions of dollars to the projects, which have attracted Chinese customers such as#TikTok owner ByteDance and Alibaba.

The new rules, which came into effect last Thursday, require data centre operators in five countries — Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil — that supply significant processing power to Chinese customers to obtain special licences from the US government to buy advanced American chips.

Washington is expected to assess which Chinese companies will have access to the chips and then decide whether to grant the licences based on how they plan to use the computing power. Operators have 90 days to obtain the licences.

Analysts expect the US to reject companies that plan to use chips to train large language models, as Washington seeks to slow down Beijing in the AI race."

Ask a senior candidate who taught them the job. Then ask who they have taught.

The second question tells you more. A leader who has developed people can name them, say what changed, and tell you where those people work now. A leader who has only managed people talks about headcount.

When we assess senior candidates, we listen for that difference. A company that hires leaders who teach fills more of its senior roles from inside. A company that doesn't goes back to the market for every senior seat.

To the teachers across Indonesia, and to the managers who teach without the title, terima kasih.

At the executive level, boards’re hiring someone to navigate ambiguity, spot blind spots, and make high-stakes trade-offs.

​Most C-suite interviews quietly derail in the first 15 minutes because the candidate spends their energy proving they can run a function (like a senior manager) rather than proving they can steward the business (like an owner).

​Owners don’t prescribe before they diagnose.
​Instead of leading with answers, the sharpest executives lead with calibrated questions that get beneath the polished pitch deck:
- ​"Where is the biggest gap between how the company looks externally and how it operates internally?"
- ​"What tough call has been delayed over the last two quarters, and what’s holding it back?"
- ​"If cash burn had to tighten by 20% tomorrow, what would break first?"

​Notice what happens when you ask questions like these: the dynamic shifts immediately from an interrogation to a peer-level strategy session. You stop auditioning for a seat at the table and start acting like you’re already accountable for the P&L.

Which side do you lean toward in final rounds: wanting to see a structured 90-day roadmap, or testing how well a candidate diagnoses the business first?

🚀 Built & Deployed an Enterprise IT Service Desk Backend with Java 17 & Spring Boot 3!
Over the past week, I took on a 7-day engineering challenge to design, build, test, and deploy a production-grade IT Service Desk REST API from scratch.
Today, the project is 100% complete, containerized, and LIVE on the internet! 🌐
---
🧪 Test the Live Application in your browser:
🔗 Swagger UI: https://lnkd.in/gj3UkHhk
💓 Health Check: https://lnkd.in/gvsGTjdC
Pre-seeded test accounts:
👤 Admin: admin / admin123 (Full privileges & ticket deletion)
🛠️ IT Support: john_support / engineer123 (Triage, assign, notes)
💼 Employee: alice_employee / employee123 (Raise & track tickets)
📂 GitHub Repository (Full Source Code & Architecture):
👉 https://lnkd.in/g779NCpu
---
🏗️ Key Engineering Implementations:
1️⃣ Clean Modular Architecture:
Strict separation of concerns across Controllers, Services, Repositories, and DTOs with Jakarta Bean Validation. Decoupled API contracts from database entities to prevent domain leakage.
2️⃣ Enterprise Security & RBAC:
Configured Spring Security 6 with salted BCrypt password hashing and stateless JWT (HMAC-SHA512) authentication. Implemented fine-grained Role-Based Access Control enforcing distinct permissions for Employees, IT Support Engineers, and Admins.
3️⃣ Automated Testing & Developer Experience:
- Service layer unit tests with JUnit 5 & Mockito covering critical workflows and custom exceptions (100% pass rate).
- Self-documenting APIs via SpringDoc OpenAPI 3 / Swagger UI with integrated JWT Bearer authorization directly in the browser.
4️⃣ DevOps & Edge Deployment:
- Multi-stage Dockerfile (Eclipse Temurin 17 JRE with a non-root application user for container security).
- Orchestrated with Docker Compose alongside a health-checked MySQL 8 database.
- Deployed live to Cloudflare’s global edge network via Cloudflare Tunnel with end-to-end TLS encryption.
---
💡 Architectural Reflections & Scaling Roadmap:
I architected this as a Clean Modular Monolith to avoid premature microservice latency. The system is cloud-native and ready to scale:
- Performance: Ready for Redis caching on hot lookup data (support categories) and token blacklisting.
- API Defense: Configurable with Bucket4j or Cloudflare WAF for rate limiting against brute-force attacks.
- Microservices Evolution: Domain modules can easily be extracted into standalone services behind a Spring Cloud Gateway with Netflix Eureka / K8s CoreDNS and Resilience4j circuit breakers.
Huge thanks to everyone who supported my journey! On to the next build. 💻
